rows.failurePoint: Request cannot be proven to have reached handler (network loss, timeout, abort); frontend init failure before push is a separate no-push path.
rows.currentDb: No push mutation effect can be inferred if request never reached push; if transport outcome is unknown, server may still be executing.
rows.receipt: Unknown until queried; no per-key query exists.
rows.httpClient: Axios timeout is 30s; no-response errors become ApiError network failure.
rows.idb: push throw exits result loop; outbox is not deleted in catch.
rows.currentNextAction: A later sync resends the persisted outbox record with same clientMutationId and current stored fields.
rows.proposedContract: Keep exact original key and payload/hash; retry same immutable command or query key-scoped outcome. Never mint a new key while outcome is unknown.
rows.lastDurableCopy: Client outbox row remains; server outcome unknown.

rows.failurePoint: Before per-item loop: device upsert, visibility read, or receipt prefetch fails.
rows.currentDb: Device upsert at sync.js:348 may already have persisted; no per-item business mutation has started.
rows.receipt: No new per-item receipt has been written by this request.
rows.httpClient: 500 is surfaced as ApiError; no automatic 5xx replay.
rows.idb: Outbox remains because push rejects before results are iterated.
rows.currentNextAction: Retry the same queued commands; no key-specific status query.
rows.proposedContract: Return/lookup explicit per-command outcome by immutable key. For failures before any command executes, retain client last copy and safely retry same key/hash.
rows.lastDurableCopy: Client outbox; device metadata may also be present server-side.

rows.failurePoint: Item is malformed (missing key/entity/id), or entity validation/access/permission rejects before mutation.
rows.currentDb: No business mutation for malformed or denied item. Access/validation outcomes inside try become rejected.
rows.receipt: Malformed item at sync.js:379-382 continues without persisting SyncMutation; ordinary rejected item is upserted as a receipt at 546-567.
rows.httpClient: If complete 200 response arrives, per-item rejected is treated as definitive by client.
rows.idb: Rejected response moves a keyed row to deadLetters and removes it in one IDB transaction; if response is lost, original outbox remains.
rows.currentNextAction: Missing-field item can be repeatedly rejected without a receipt; ordinary rejection retry is re-evaluated and can overwrite the same global key record.
rows.proposedContract: Every accepted command key must have durable terminal/pending outcome, including malformed keyed commands where safe; bind actor/device/key/hash; reject changed payload/actor.
rows.lastDurableCopy: On delivered reject: deadLetter plus atomic outbox removal. On response loss: outbox.

rows.failurePoint: Business operation errors before commit / transactional subcommand rolls back.
rows.currentDb: Expected operation-specific rollback where the command itself uses a transaction (e.g. task compound changes at sync.js:479-491); not all entity operations share a single outer transaction.
rows.receipt: Caught error is converted to rejected/conflict; then a separate SyncMutation upsert is attempted. If it succeeds, response contains per-item result.
rows.httpClient: A full result response is processed; outer receipt failure or later failure produces 500 instead.
rows.idb: Rejected is moved atomically to deadLetters; conflict is removed from outbox and accumulated for local conflict state.
rows.currentNextAction: Same-key replay of applied only; rejected/conflict entries are reprocessed and their global receipt overwritten.
rows.proposedContract: Atomically persist command decision and outcome; stable key/hash semantics make retries deterministic. Last local copy must be committed before removing outbox.
rows.lastDurableCopy: For delivered rejection: deadLetters. For conflict: server SyncMutation may persist, but local deletion precedes final conflict kvSet (see FP-09).

rows.failurePoint: Business mutation commits, then SyncMutation upsert fails (B06).
rows.currentDb: Business write can be committed; historical task probe observed committed title despite HTTP 500. Other entity/op effects vary: stale-base updates may later conflict; no-base updates may reapply; create may collide; tombstone/delete may repeat. No generic at-most-once claim.
rows.receipt: Absent or previous record remains because separate upsert failed.
rows.httpClient: Outer error becomes HTTP 500; client receives no per-item results.
rows.idb: Original mutation row remains; retry uses same clientMutationId, entity/op/id/data/baseUpdatedAt from outbox.
rows.currentNextAction: If receipt absent, current server processes again; generic query route is absent. Results are operation-specific and may diverge from original attempt.
rows.proposedContract: One DB commit boundary for authorization/CAS/business/audit/scoped receipt; unknown result resolved by exact-key/exact-hash status lookup or exact immutable same-key retry.
rows.lastDurableCopy: Client outbox plus mutated server business row; this is the proven ambiguity.

rows.failurePoint: Earlier item receipt persisted; a later item receipt write fails before batch completes.
rows.currentDb: Earlier business mutations and receipts persist independently; failing item may also have its business mutation committed; later items are not processed. Batch is sequential and has no encompassing transaction.
rows.receipt: Earlier receipts persist; failing item receipt may be absent; later item receipts absent.
rows.httpClient: Outer 500 returns no partial results array.
rows.idb: All original outbox rows remain because response promise rejects before result processing.
rows.currentNextAction: Retry resubmits entire batch: earlier applied receipts are replayed; missing receipt items reprocess; later items execute for first time.
rows.proposedContract: Specify per-command outcome despite batch interruption; per-item atomic receipt and exact replay. Do not promise batch atomicity.
rows.lastDurableCopy: Client retains batch records; server may hold partial business/receipt state.

rows.failurePoint: All item receipts persisted, then lastPushAt update fails before response; aggregate audit insert failures are caught by writeAudit and do not ordinarily cause 500.
rows.currentDb: Business writes and per-item receipts may all be durable; lastPushAt update may fail. writeAudit catches DB insert failures and logs them, so those alone do not fail the request; invalid audit action normalization could throw, but this route supplies the fixed valid UPDATE constant.
rows.receipt: Per-item receipt rows have already been written.
rows.httpClient: A failure of the uncaught lastPushAt update yields 500/no usable results. Audit insert errors are swallowed and normally still permit 200 response.
rows.idb: Outbox remains if the request fails before the response promise resolves; if response arrives normally, per-item outcomes are processed.
rows.currentNextAction: For lastPushAt failure, retry normally hits applied receipts and replays their stored results. Aggregate audit insertion failure does not require a retry because request continues.
rows.proposedContract: Response loss resolves from scoped durable result; required per-command audit is inside the same command commit boundary. Keep aggregate best-effort audit semantics explicitly separate if retained.
rows.lastDurableCopy: After lastPushAt failure: server receipts plus client outbox. If aggregate audit insert fails but response succeeds, result processing proceeds normally.

rows.failurePoint: Receipt committed and response sent, but response is lost in network or client times out.
rows.receipt: Stored result exists if all item writes completed.
rows.httpClient: A no-response timeout/network error is thrown; 5xx is surfaced, not automatically retried.
rows.currentNextAction: Next manual/online sync resubmits same key. Applied record replays if still retained; no expiry/retention policy is proven for SyncMutation in this review.
rows.proposedContract: Scoped outcome lookup or same-key/hash replay within published retention. Beyond retention, unknown/expired remains held for recovery; never silently re-key.
rows.lastDurableCopy: Server receipt and client outbox; after server retention expires, only client outbox may remain.

rows.failurePoint: A 200 response is received, but client crashes midway through per-result local processing.
rows.currentDb: Per-item receipts remain for processed commands, subject to retention.
rows.receipt: Applied/conflict/rejected records are stored by server before response except malformed items without key/receipt.
rows.httpClient: Response resolved; engine processes items sequentially.
rows.idb: Applied: server receipt permits replay after outbox deletion. Rejected: deadLetterMove atomically stores copy then deletes outbox. Conflict: outbox is deleted immediately, but merged conflict list is persisted only after the whole loop; a crash between delete and kvSet can leave no local copy (server receipt is not available by-key through current API).
rows.currentNextAction: Recovery differs by per-result status; omitted results are not deleted and stay in outbox because runtime validates neither response completeness nor request/result key-set equality.
rows.proposedContract: For every status, atomically retain a local outcome copy before outbox deletion; validate complete key-set and expose server lookup.
rows.lastDurableCopy: For conflict there is a possible client last-copy gap; server DB receipt exists but not client-visible by key.

rows.failurePoint: SyncMutation row is later expired/deleted or request retry falls outside actual retention window.
rows.currentDb: Schema has createdAt but no expiry field; external cleanup job/effective retention was not checked and remains S03-OI-04.
rows.receipt: Historical S03 static review found no cleanup in push path; deployment/ops cleanup remains unknown.
rows.httpClient: No key-specific lookup; `/sync/status` reports aggregate counts only.
rows.idb: Outbox/deadletter row may remain locally, but no expiry protocol or re-key guard is established by this path.
rows.currentNextAction: Cannot infer whether retry replays or reprocesses after cleanup.
rows.proposedContract: Expose explicit retained/expired/unknown per key; preserve original key/hash and last local copy; expired/unknown blocks automatic re-key/replay pending authorized recovery.
rows.lastDurableCopy: Client outbox/deadletter if retained; effective server receipt retention unknown.

crossCutting.issue: Current `clientMutationId` uniqueness is global, not scoped; SyncMutation has no payload hash or immutable actor binding.
crossCutting.implication: Existing applied replay can cross payload/actor boundaries per historical B05; no same-key-different-hash/actor protection is proven.

crossCutting.issue: /sync/status returns device metadata and aggregate mutation/conflict counts only.
crossCutting.implication: It cannot resolve a particular clientMutationId or distinguish unknown/expired/applied.

crossCutting.issue: No runtime response completeness assertion compares submitted keys to returned results.
crossCutting.implication: A returned response missing an expected item result leaves that submitted outbox row queued; duplicate/unexpected result handling has no explicit protocol contract.

crossCutting.issue: PC03 proposes same-transaction business/audit/scoped receipt and exact-key/hash unknown recovery; status remains PROPOSED.
crossCutting.implication: This matrix defines a recommended static contract only; it is not approval, implementation, dynamic acceptance, or release evidence.

recommendedStaticRecoveryContract: Each mutation is immutable after first send: actor/user, device, clientMutationId, entity/op/id, canonical payload hash, and base revision are bound and persisted.
Authorization revalidation, CAS, business change, required audit, and scoped result receipt commit atomically per command; the batch is not promised atomic.

For unknown outcome, clients may query by authenticated actor + original mutationId and verify original payload hash, or retry the exact same immutable key/hash; changed actor/hash is rejected without side effects.
Every known terminal result is queryable by key. A missing/expired result is explicit UNKNOWN_OR_EXPIRED; it does not authorize new-key replay.

Client writes returned applied/conflict/rejected outcome to a durable owner-scoped result store before removing the outbox row; rejected dead-letter and outbox move remain one transaction; conflict needs equivalent atomic retention.
Keep original local copy while outcome is unknown or expired; manual/business recovery decides next action. No silent re-key, payload mutation, or deletion.
Per-item receipts survive later batch item failures; clients can resolve each item independently. No all-or-nothing batch promise.
Publish receipt retention duration and the longest supported offline window before relying on retry semantics.
